reason: The cited evidence directly shows a high-temperature strength plateau (E1), edge-dislocation-dominant deformation (E2, E3), and a contrast with conventional screw-dominated BCC behavior (E3), supporting the core premises. However, the specific causal link between lattice distortion and edge-dislocation stabilization via solid-solution strengthening is inferred rather than directly demonstrated, and the role of thermal super-jogging is only mentioned as speculation in E1.
premises: Large lattice distortion and chemical complexity in single-phase refractory HEAs stabilize edge over screw dislocations at high temperature.
This edge-dislocation dominance produces a solid-solution strengthening effect that limits thermal softening.
The mechanism involves thermal super-jogging and glide of edge dislocations.
The predicted outcome is a strength plateau and reduced temperature sensitivity of elastic moduli compared to conventional BCC alloys.
The hypothesis applies only to homogeneous, single-phase refractory HEAs under controlled conditions.
